title: Endpoint isolation — EDR isolate with network-ACL fallback
summary: Containment control that severs an implicated endpoint from the production network as the first concrete mitigation in a ransomware response. Primary path issues an EDR-native isolate action (host quarantine: kernel-level network gate, only EDR management plane reachable). Fallback path drops a network-ACL deny at the access switch / SDN policy plane when the EDR agent is unreachable or unhealthy. The control couples preventive boundary protection (D3-NTF Network Traffic Filtering) with reactive host quarantine and is the single feature most ransomware-response playbooks pivot on once triage confirms the event.

component.title: Endpoint isolation control
component.description: EDR-administered host isolation with network-ACL fallback at the access boundary.

control-implementations.description: Implements incident-response containment, boundary protection, and information-flow restriction during a confirmed event.

implemented-requirements.description: Incident handling — containment via host quarantine on confirmed events.
Incident handling | automated incident handling processes — EDR-driven isolate action.
Boundary protection — network-ACL fallback at the access boundary when the EDR isolate path is unavailable.
Information flow enforcement — only management-plane flows are permitted to and from the quarantined host.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 — IR-4 Incident Handling, IR-4(1), SC-7 Boundary Protection, AC-4 Information Flow Enforcement
